text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000054 bills 99215 at a flat high rate regardless of patient complexity, mostly on patients with simple diagnoses, though too few charts came back to confirm upcoding.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The strongest signal is the complexity breakdown: this provider's 99215 share stays near the same level for patients with 0, 1 or 2 conditions, while the all-provider share rises with complexity, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s are mostly routine diagnoses such as UTI (N39.0), rash (R21), upper respiratory infection (J06.9) and follow-up (Z09). That pattern is consistent with upcoding rather than with a sicker panel. The documentation is too thin to settle the question, because only five 99215 charts were reviewed. Two of those five, including C0028397 (single-condition obesity visit), were documented at moderate MDM, which is suggestive but not conclusive at this sample size. The supported examples also deserve a look, since C0028365 is a URI visit on a patient with no chronic conditions that was documented as high MDM, so the reviewer should check that note for cloned or templated content. First, request more charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims (for example C0028361, C0028415, C0028433, C0028521) and compare the documented MDM and time against the diagnoses and the services on each claim."}
